claims.statement: For any two fixed affine two-state Markov occupancy maps F_A(x)=a_A x+b_A and F_B(x)=a_B x+b_B, the endpoint occupancy contrast F_B(F_A(x))-F_A(F_B(x))=(a_B-1)b_A+(1-a_A)b_B is independent of the initial occupancy x. A common terminal observation channel maps this to an outcome-law contrast proportional to the hidden occupancy contrast, including common read transitions and backgrounds.
assumptions: Hidden state is exactly two-state and transition dynamics are Markovian at the declared state resolution
The A/B waveform maps are stable and identical in their AB and BA uses
Terminal read conditional laws L0,L1 are common across order arms
The endpoint statistic or total-variation separation has a nonzero state read contrast
claims.novelty: UNKNOWN. Affine pulse-order algebra and force-dependent HJ HMM analyses are prior art; no priority claim is made for this endpoint formulation.
claims.costs: One independent molecule per endpoint record in the conservative design. Pairing independent bounded [0,1] outcomes across arms gives n>=8 log(2/alpha)/g^2 per order arm for both errors <=alpha. Add pilot, blank, force telemetry, and molecule-capture costs; those are not sourced.
claims.falsifier: A two-state affine map counterexample with initial-state-dependent AB-BA occupancy contrast, or a stable common-read controlled experiment whose endpoint law violates proportionality to that contrast.
claims.next_gate: Acquire time-tagged force and photon records under randomized AB/BA loops; estimate ramp maps, state-read contrast, background, and force-history dependence.

claims.statement: When an A loop consists of fixed pre/post ramp Markov maps around an A plateau of duration s, while a B loop duration is fixed, the order contrast is C0+C1 exp(-lambda_A s). Three equally spaced duration contrasts D0,D1,D2 with nonzero curvature satisfy (D2-D1)/(D1-D0)=exp(-lambda_A tau), so lambda_A is identified without knowing initial occupancy, equilibrium occupancies, fixed ramp maps, or terminal emission amplitude.
assumptions: Two-state homogeneous CTMC at each plateau force, with lambda_A=k01(A)+k10(A)
Pre/post A ramp waveforms do not change with plateau duration or sequence position
B loop is fixed across the three durations
Terminal channel is common and has nonzero contrast
Duration curvature coefficient C1 is nonzero and signs can be oriented
claims.novelty: UNKNOWN. Three-point exponential ratio/Prony system identification is classical; the possible contribution is the force-loop endpoint interface under common unknown readout, which has not had a priority search.
claims.costs: Six treatment arms (three durations by two orders); finite Hoeffding rate inversion can require tens of millions of independent endpoint records per arm at the illustrative HJ-scale contrast. HMM full traces may dominate.
claims.falsifier: Held-out same-molecule duration contrasts that fail a single exponential with fixed ramp maps, or force-loop curvature C1 too small to resolve at declared costs.
claims.next_gate: Compare full photon-likelihood estimates against the endpoint ratio at equal photon dose and force time; require two-state residual checks and report UNKNOWN under kinetic-class sign cancellation.

claims.statement: A force intervention with different stationary occupancies at A and B can create an O(kappa) endpoint output gap under a weak kappa reporter and hence O(kappa^2) endpoint KL, while the c4 full-transcript lower bound is O(kappa^4) only for fixed-uniform-stationary doubly stochastic action kernels. An explicit two-state pair has passive C-only laws equal and nonzero AB/BA contrast under active forces.
assumptions: Same common C generator and same initial law in candidate worlds
The alternative A/B inputs have pi_A != pi_B; the null does not
A weak known binary reporter has contrast kappa
Endpoint outputs across randomized molecules are independent at the superpopulation level
claims.novelty: The exponent separation follows from leaving the lower-bound action class; this is not a counterexample to its theorem or an external novelty claim.
claims.costs: For the explicit witness, the order-arm gap is about 0.2398*kappa and the conservative paired-difference Hoeffding count is about 514*kappa^-2 at alpha=0.05. At kappa=0.1 this is about 51,400 records per arm; the c4 lower-bound constant is weak at that point.
claims.falsifier: A proposed physical control whose stationary law is in fact common across force levels, or a measured endpoint channel with no detectable order contrast at the stated exposure cost.
claims.next_gate: Quantify whether force-dependent equilibrium shifts and terminal photon contrast are large enough in the actual HJ geometry; compare with full-likelihood active acquisition.

claims.statement: In the no-ramp two-state contiguous AB/BA model with sA+sB=T fixed, the absolute hidden occupancy order gap is |piB-piA|(1-exp(-lambdaA*sA))(1-exp(-lambdaB*sB)); its unique maximum equates lambdaA/(exp(lambdaA*sA)-1) and lambdaB/(exp(lambdaB*sB)-1). For a fixed bounded read gap, this minimizes the distribution-free Hoeffding endpoint bound within this schedule family.
assumptions: Two-state homogeneous CTMC at A and B
No ramps, or ramp overhead independent of the dwell split for this stated formula
Contiguous AB/BA comparison with fixed total plateau dwell
Known rates for selecting the optimum, with any pilot cost charged separately
A common terminal bounded read channel across order arms
claims.novelty: UNKNOWN. The optimization is elementary within the restricted model and is not a global optimal-control or photon-information result.
claims.costs: Synthetic T=2 s scenario at rates 0.5 and 2 per second lowers a bounded-read per-arm Hoeffding count from 709 to 629; actual ramp calibration and pilot molecule costs are unknown.
claims.falsifier: A within-model split with larger endpoint gap at the same total dwell, or an empirical calibrated-ramp design whose optimum is incorrectly predicted by the no-ramp equation.
claims.next_gate: Use calibrated loop affine maps and a pilot-funded design to compare the best-split endpoint statistic with full photon-arrival CTMC/HMM likelihood under identical photon, molecule, force-time, and blank budgets.

claims.statement: A physically proposed HJ assay uses existing optical-tweezer/smFRET hardware to apply repeated force loops in the dark, return to one common read force C, and collect a short terminal FRET read after randomized AB or BA. This is a proposed acquisition protocol, not a reported or validated experiment.
assumptions: Piezo force trajectories can be measured and repeated at required timescales
Confocal excitation is shuttered during loops and tracks the molecule as in the source setup
The force order does not irreversibly change the construct or its terminal dye channel
A low-dose common endpoint read has usable conditional state contrast
claims.novelty: UNKNOWN. Force-pulse protocols, HJ force-smFRET, and HMM kinetic fits exist. The proposed combination of dark pulse loops and common endpoint randomized order has not been priority-cleared.
claims.costs: Charge three independent cost streams: founder count per endpoint arm, waveform wall time/force calibration, and photons/background blanking. Source photon rates and ramp settling are absent, so absolute time, laser dose, and expected photons are UNKNOWN.
claims.falsifier: AB/BA terminal contrast disappears under common force/read calibration, or its apparent effect is reproduced by no-tether/fluorophore controls or force-path differences.
claims.next_gate: Pilot exact waveform repeatability, background, photon arrivals, dye-history controls, and full-likelihood matched comparator before any claim of practical information gain.

overall_verdict: Useful conditional measurement invariant, restricted fixed-budget dwell optimizer, and explicit action-class escape from the internal uniform-stationary lower bound; physical acquisition advantage over a matched active full-likelihood HMM is unproven and probably not present. Endpoint rate inversion is sample-expensive. External novelty and physical transfer remain UNKNOWN.
